proposals.before: In the Taishi era he was named director of retainers for Jinxi, gentleman of the ministry of personnel's promotions section, and unimpeded-attendant gentleman.
proposals.after: In the Taishi era he was named director of retainers for Jinxi, gentleman of the ministry of works, and unimpeded-attendant gentleman.
proposals.reason: 尚書起部郎 is the gentleman of the Board of Works (起部), not the ministry of personnel's promotions section.

proposals.before: In the Taishi era he was appointed director of retainers for the Jinxi state, gentleman of the ministry of personnel's promotions section, and unimpeded-attendant gentleman.
proposals.after: In the Taishi era he was appointed director of retainers for the Jinxi state, gentleman of the ministry of works, and unimpeded-attendant gentleman.
proposals.reason: 尚書起部郎 is the gentleman of the Board of Works (起部), not the ministry of personnel's promotions section.

proposals.before: In the second year of Jianyuan he issued an edict the court ministers: "The yellow register is the people's great charter and the state's hinge of order.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan he issued an edict to the court ministers: "The yellow register is the people's great charter and the state's hinge of order.
proposals.reason: English omits the preposition 'to' before 'the court ministers', producing ungrammatical prose.

proposals.before: In the second year of Jianyuan he issued an edict the court ministers: "The yellow register is the people's great charter and the state's hinge of order.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan he issued an edict to the court ministers: "The yellow register is the people's great charter and the state's hinge of order.
proposals.reason: English omits the preposition 'to' before 'the court ministers', producing ungrammatical prose.

proposals.before: Of forty-two brothers who shared the deepest mourning bond, through fortune and ruin, long life and early death, I alone remain.
proposals.after: Of forty-two brothers of the same dagong (second-degree) mourning grade, through fortune and ruin, long life and early death, I alone remain.
proposals.reason: 大功 denotes the second-degree mourning grade for collateral kin, not the deepest mourning bond.

proposals.before: Without scheming for preferment I rose to the nine ministers; in virtue I am no Li Ling, yet I hold a post at the gate.
proposals.after: Without scheming for preferment I rose to the nine ministers; in virtue I am ashamed before Li Ling, yet I presumptuously hold a Menxia post.
proposals.reason: 德慙李陵 means ashamed before Li Ling, not identity denial; 門下 is the Menxia office.

proposals.before: I passed through dark reigns and trampled chaos, forded hardship and walked on danger; I looked up to sage virtue to keep myself whole and leaned on worthy aides to hold my station. I never tired of bending before merit and power, never feared drowning among foxes and rats—yet the ground I stand on has not given way.
proposals.after: I passed through dark reigns and trampled chaos, forded hardship and walked on danger; I looked up to sage virtue to keep myself whole and leaned on worthy aides to hold my station. I never demeaned myself by yielding to merit and power, never feared drowning among foxes and rats—and the ground I stand on has not given way.
proposals.reason: 未嘗厭屈於勳權 means he never abased himself before the powerful; never tired of bending reverses the sense.

proposals.before: Xiu first served as Commandant of the Horse Fleet, Court Attendant for Imperial Audiences, and regular attendant in Prince Xiangdong's establishment under Emperor Ming of Song.
proposals.after: Xiu first served as Commandant-escort for Imperial Princesses (驸马都尉), Court Attendant for Imperial Audiences, and regular attendant in the Xiangdong establishment of (the future) Emperor Ming of Song.
proposals.reason: 駙馬都尉 is the imperial son-in-law / princess-escort commandant, not a 'Horse Fleet' command; 宋明帝湘東國 means the Xiangdong princely household of the man who became Emperor Ming.

proposals.before: Xiu first served as Commandant of the Horse Fleet, Court Attendant for Imperial Audiences, and regular attendant in Prince Xiangdong's establishment under Emperor Ming of Song.
proposals.after: Xiu first served as Commandant-escort for Imperial Princesses, Court Attendant for Imperial Audiences, and regular attendant of Emperor Ming of Song's Xiangdong establishment.
proposals.reason: Same 駙馬都尉 mistranslation as in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: Emperor Shun was the son of the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan.
proposals.after: Emperor Shun was the son of the Prince of Guiyang, Xiufan.
proposals.reason: 休範 is the single given name Xiufan, not two names 'Xiu Fan'.

proposals.before: Yan Yuan answered without thinking, "As Your Majesty wills."
proposals.after: Yanyuan answered without thinking, "As Your Majesty wills."
proposals.reason: 彥遠 is the given name Yanyuan; splitting it as 'Yan Yuan' invents a wrong English form.

proposals.before: When Shen Youzhi rose, Emperor Xiaowu took the joint army headquarters of the princes at Pencheng; Xiu handled military funds. After peace returned he became the Prince of Shaoling's pacification-of-the-south chief aide, then yellow gate officer, Ningshuo general, front-army chief aide, and Qi platform regular attendant.
proposals.after: When Shen Youzhi rose, the World-Ancestor (Emperor Wu of Qi) took the Jinxi and Shaoling princely headquarters and garrisoned Pencheng; Xiu handled military funds. After peace returned he became the Prince of Shaoling's pacification-of-the-south chief aide, then yellow gate officer, Ningshuo general, front-army chief aide, and Qi platform regular attendant.
proposals.reason: In the Nan Qi Shu, 世祖 is Emperor Wu of Qi, not Emperor Xiaowu of Song; 挾晉熙邵陵二王軍府鎮盆城 means he took those two princes' headquarters to garrison Pencheng.

proposals.before: During Shen Youzhi's rebellion, Emperor Xiaowu seized the military headquarters of the two princes at Pencheng; Xiu managed military expenses; when the matter was settled, he was moved to the Prince of Shaoling's Pacification of the South chief aide, made Yellow Gate Officer, Ningshuo general, front army chief aide, and Qi Platform Regular Attendant.
proposals.after: During Shen Youzhi's rebellion, the World-Ancestor (Emperor Wu of Qi) took the military headquarters of the Princes of Jinxi and Shaoling and garrisoned Pencheng; Xiu managed military expenses; when the matter was settled, he was moved to the Prince of Shaoling's Pacification of the South chief aide, made Yellow Gate Officer, Ningshuo general, front army chief aide, and Qi Platform Regular Attendant.
proposals.reason: Same 世祖 misidentification and omission of 晉熙邵陵 as in the idiomatic line.

proposals.before: As for my presumptuous excess, I should request bones and flesh."
proposals.after: As for my presumptuous excess, I should ask leave to resign and return home."
proposals.reason: 乞骸骨 is the conventional resignation formula 'request [to return] my bones,' not a literal request for bones and flesh.

proposals.before: Under Yuankang, Yang Xin took up Zi Jing's standard clerical hand and the world bowed to it; the Right General's manner, a little old-fashioned, was no longer valued.
proposals.after: Under Yuanjia, Yang Xin took up Zi Jing's standard clerical hand and the world bowed to it; the Right General's manner, a little old-fashioned, was no longer valued.
proposals.reason: Chinese 元嘉 is Yuanjia, not Yuankang; the packet reign list also identifies 元嘉 as Yuanjia.

proposals.before: In the Yuankang era Yang Xin received Zi Jing's orthodox clerical method; the age together honored it; the Right General's style was slightly archaic and no longer prized.
proposals.after: In the Yuanjia era Yang Xin received Zi Jing's orthodox clerical method; the age together honored it; the Right General's style was slightly archaic and no longer prized.
proposals.reason: Chinese 元嘉 must be rendered Yuanjia, not Yuankang.

proposals.before: Under Yuankang he went out as secretary on the Prince of Jin'an's pacification of the west, came back as Situ chief clerk and magistrate of Shanyin, then became Situ recorder.
proposals.after: Under Yuanhui he went out as secretary on the Prince of Jin'an's pacification of the west, came back as Situ chief clerk and magistrate of Shanyin, then became Situ recorder.
proposals.reason: Chinese 元徽 is Yuanhui, not Yuankang.

proposals.before: In the Yuankang period he was sent out as Prince of Jin'an's Pacification of the West secretary, returned as Situ chief clerk and Magistrate of Shanyin, and transferred to Situ recorder staff officer.
proposals.after: In the Yuanhui period he was sent out as Prince of Jin'an's Pacification of the West secretary, returned as Situ chief clerk and Magistrate of Shanyin, and transferred to Situ recorder staff officer.
proposals.reason: Chinese 元徽 is Yuanhui, not Yuankang.

proposals.before: When the crown prince's son of Luling held Yingzhou, Chong served as his chief clerk, assisting-state general, and Jiangxia interior minister, running headquarters and provincial business.
proposals.after: When Champion General, Prince of Luling, Ziqing held Yingzhou, Chong served as his chief clerk, assisting-state general, and Jiangxia interior minister, running headquarters and provincial business.
proposals.reason: 冠軍廬陵王子卿 means Champion General and Prince of Luling, personal name Ziqing; 子卿 is not 'crown prince's son', and he held Yingzhou rather than being 'prince of Yingzhou'.

proposals.before: The crown-prince's son of Luling, prince of Yingzhou, had Chong as chief clerk, assisting-state general, and Jiangxia interior minister, acting on headquarters and province affairs.
proposals.after: Champion General, Prince of Luling Ziqing, for Yingzhou, had Chong as chief clerk, assisting-state general, and Jiangxia interior minister, acting on headquarters and province affairs.
proposals.reason: 子卿 is the personal name Ziqing; 爲郢州 means he was assigned Yingzhou, not that he was prince of Yingzhou.

proposals.before: In Yongming, Yuan impeached Yuan Yi, grand administrator of Wu; in Jianwu, Yi's cousin's son Ang took the censor's seat and, within days, struck at Yuan's son Hui for letting his father travel in a hired white-canopy carriage—Hui was cashiered and barred from office.
proposals.after: In Yongming, Yuan impeached Yuan Tuan, grand administrator of Wuxing; in Jianwu, Tuan's younger cousin Ang took the censor's seat and, within days, struck at Yuan's son Hui for letting his father travel in a hired white-canopy carriage—Hui was cashiered and barred from office.
proposals.reason: 袁彖 is Yuan Tuan (not Yi); 吳興 is Wuxing; 從弟 is a younger cousin, not a cousin's son.

proposals.before: In Yongming Yuan impeached Yuan Yi, grand administrator of Wu commandery; in Jianwu Yi's cousin's son Ang became censor, and within days of taking office memorialized against Yuan's son Hui because his father rode in a rented white-canopy carriage—Hui was dismissed and forbidden from office.
proposals.after: In Yongming Yuan impeached Yuan Tuan, grand administrator of Wuxing commandery; in Jianwu Tuan's younger cousin Ang became censor, and within days of taking office memorialized against Yuan's son Hui because his father rode in a rented white-canopy carriage—Hui was dismissed and forbidden from office.
proposals.reason: Correct 袁彖 to Yuan Tuan, 吳興 to Wuxing, and 從弟 to younger cousin.

proposals.before: The heir apparent had him receive the barbarian envoys, with added rank as attendant-in-ordinary.
proposals.after: The emperor ordered him to receive the barbarian envoys, with added rank as attendant-in-ordinary.
proposals.reason: At this career stage 世祖 denotes Emperor Wu of Qi by temple name, not the heir apparent; following units already call him 上/帝.

proposals.before: The heir apparent ordered him to face the barbarian envoys, with added rank as attendant-in-ordinary.
proposals.after: The emperor ordered him to face the barbarian envoys, with added rank as attendant-in-ordinary.
proposals.reason: Same 世祖 referent: reigning emperor in this narrative context, not heir apparent.

proposals.before: The emperor often sighed over the grace of his person; Wang Jian, seated beside him, said: "Set Gaozhi's cicada crown under the throne's radiance and his bearing only grows brighter.
proposals.after: The emperor often sighed over the grace of his person; Wang Jian, seated beside him, said: "When Gaozhi is illuminated by the cicada crown, his bearing only grows brighter.
proposals.reason: English invents an imperative and obscures 為蟬冕所照, which means Gaozhi is lit or enhanced by the cicada-crown office.

proposals.before: He lived in poverty by choice; his table held only chive pickle, vinegared chives, raw chives, and humble greens. A wit said: "Who calls Minister Yu poor? When he dines on salmon he still has twenty-seven kinds."
proposals.after: He lived in poverty by choice; his table held only chive pickle, vinegared chives, raw chives, and humble greens. A wit said: "Who calls Minister Yu poor? When he dines on fish dishes he still has twenty-seven kinds."
proposals.reason: 鮭 in the classic three-chives joke is a general fish-dish term, not specifically salmon.

proposals.before: Emperor Wu of Qi had known Chen in Emperor Ming of Song's reign and meant to use him well: aide to the state, chief staff officer to the Prince of Jin'an's southern center, grand administrator of Huainan, running headquarters and province.
proposals.after: Emperor Wu of Qi had known Chen in Emperor Ming of Song's reign and meant to entrust him with office: General Who Assists the State, chief staff officer to the Prince of Jin'an's Southern Household Gentleman command, grand administrator of Huainan, acting for the headquarters and province.
proposals.reason: 輔國將軍 is a general's title, not merely 'aide to the state'; 南中郎 is the Southern Household Gentleman command, not 'southern center'.

proposals.before: The Shizu emperor had known Chen in Ming of Song's time and wished to entrust him; he was made aide to the state, chief staff officer to the Prince of Jin'an's southern center, and grand administrator of Huainan, acting for headquarters and province.
proposals.after: The Shizu emperor had known Chen in Ming of Song's time and wished to entrust him; he was made General Who Assists the State, chief staff officer to the Prince of Jin'an's Southern Household Gentleman command, and grand administrator of Huainan, acting for headquarters and province.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation: 輔國將軍 and 南中郎 should name the generalship and Southern Household Gentleman staff post.

proposals.before: To read old documents in vain only breeds the people's luck.
proposals.after: To leaf through old documents in vain only teaches the people to count on luck.
proposals.reason: 徒成民幸 means fostering opportunistic reliance on luck, not literally breeding luck.

decisions.reason: 尚書起部郎 names the Shangshu Board of Works (起部) gentleman; 'ministry of personnel's promotions section' invents the wrong bureau.

decisions.reason: 大功 is the nine-month mourning grade for collateral kin, not the deepest mourning bond. The revised wording explains the relationship without the inaccurate 'second-degree' label.
德慙李陵 is shame before Li Ling, not denial of identity; 忝居門下 is a presumptuous Menxia post, not a generic gate post.
未嘗厭屈於勳權 means he never abased himself by yielding to the powerful; 'never tired of bending' reverses 厭屈.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepting r0010 shows alternate-name Xiu Fan was created only by splitting 休範; Xiufan remains supported by c0221, so this spaced alias has no remaining source basis.
Accepting r0011 shows alternate-name Yan Yuan was invented by splitting 彥遠; the source supports only the given name Yanyuan, not this two-word form.
Accepting r0021 shows English Yuan Yi came only from the bad translation of 袁彖; the person remains Yuan Tuan (c0344), so the Yi personal-name claim has no support.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0021 restores 彖 as Tuan in the English; the personal-name claim remains valid and should be explicit rather than strongly-inferred.
